PSD12 — A TYPE ACCELERATOR NAMES A FRAMEWORK TYPE, AND THE ROW NOW SAYS SO. `[string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($x)` is `System.String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace`; `[guid]::NewGuid()` is `System.Guid.NewGuid`. The analyzer knew only the written spelling, so it published `calls -> string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace` with `ownerMemberAbsent {owner: "string"}` — a claim whose owner NO admitted file declares, which the arbiter can therefore only answer UNVERIFIED. MEASURED over the whole population before the change: 2,256 `ownerMemberAbsent` rows in `ext?`, the largest single class in that column; the claim was false in its own terms (it asserts the owner is published).

THE RESOLVED NAME IS A CITATION, NOT A GUESS. The two sources are documented and closed: PowerShell's type-accelerator table (about_Type_Accelerators) and, for the names that are not accelerators, the runtime's own type resolution — the implicit `System.` attempt and the loaded-assembly search — applied to the framework types this population names. Every entry maps to a type whose namespace-qualified name the .NET API browser states. A literal the table does NOT carry is left exactly as it was, deliberately: `[Path]` has no documented resolution (`System.Path` does not exist, and the assembly search can answer more than one `Path`), so inventing `System.Path` would be a false row — row 4 is that twin.

WHY THE TARGET AND NOT A NEW CLAIM. The row's target is a NAME, and the name it currently carries is not the thing it names. `[System.Math]::Max` already published `System.Math.Max` (PS-B22's `Type.Member` shape), so an accelerator row published as `System.String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace` is the SAME shape rather than a new vocabulary — and its root is a documented namespace, which the existing namespace claim certifies with the list as its evidence (`languageNamespace: ["System"]`). No new claim kind, no arbiter change.

THE SHADOW TWIN IS THE GUARD. PowerShell class lookup is case-insensitive, so `class Regex` in this file wins over `[regex]`: row 3 must bind in-file and must NOT be rewritten. Writing it found a real defect in the pre-existing check — `classMembers.get(staticType)` was an EXACT key read, so `[counter]::Add()` missed `class Counter` and would now have been rewritten to a framework type. The lookup is folded, and row 3 fails if it is not.

expectRelationships.comment: THE POSITIVE THE CHANGE EXISTS FOR. The written literal is kept in `typeAccelerator` (the evidence a reviewer needs to re-derive the row), the resolved type is in `staticTypeResolved`, and the target is the name the call actually reaches. The namespace claim is what the arbiter verifies — before this, the row carried a claim about `string` that nothing in the project could answer.
A second entry, so a table that happened to special-case one alias cannot pass. `guid` is a documented accelerator for `System.Guid`.

THE SHADOW TWIN. `class Regex` is declared eight lines above, so the literal names THIS FILE's class; PowerShell's class lookup does not care about the accelerator and neither may the analyzer. The row must stay in-file: no resolved type, no namespace claim.

THE UNDOCUMENTED-RESOLUTION TWIN. `System.Path` does not exist and the loaded-assembly search can answer more than one type named `Path`, so the analyzer may not invent a name for it. The row keeps exactly the treatment it had, which is the proof that the table moves only what it can cite.

THE SECOND HALF, and the shape 1,038 population rows moved with: a DOTTED literal names `System.IO.Path` through the implicit-`System.` rule, and no published symbol can be keyed by a dotted name — class names cannot contain `.` and every variable/function/parameter is stored bare. The generic externality reading is therefore a question the project can answer, and it answers by finding nothing.

THE DECLARED-SPELLING ROW. Two separate defects fail here and only here: an exact-key class lookup (which misses `counter` vs `Counter` entirely) and a target built from the LITERAL (`counter.Zero`), which the store cannot bind because the class method's qualified name is `Counter.Zero`. MEASURED over the population: six rows are exactly this shape and they moved from `ext?`/`unresolved` to RESOLVED when the declaration's spelling was published.

forbidRelationships.comment: The accelerator table must never shadow a class this file declares.
An invented resolution. The table carries ONLY documented types; `System.Path` is not one.
The pre-fix spelling. Keeping it would keep the `ownerMemberAbsent` claim whose owner no file declares.
The two claim shapes are alternatives, never companions: a row that names the framework type cannot also claim an absent member of a type the project does not declare.
The literal spelling of a declaration this file carries. The store's qualified name is the declaration's, so this target can only be an unresolvable duplicate of a call that resolves.

expectRelationshipCount.comment: The whole file: 6 `calls` (rows 1-6) and 10 `contains` (the module holds `blank`, `id`, `Regex`, `local`, `combined`, `full`, `Counter` and `zero`; `Regex` holds `Pattern` and `Counter` holds `Zero`). The count matters because two of the passes REWRITE a target rather than adding or dropping a row — an implementation that published both spellings would satisfy every expect row and fail here.
